extracted.intended_audience: students and general readers studying North Carolina history (secondary/early college level)
extracted.subtask_description: A set of study and comprehension questions appended to consecutive chapters of a North Carolina history textbook (covering the 1840s through 1861) intended to assess recall, understanding, and synthesis of chapter material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Question 1 (preceding CH. LI): What period have we now reached?
rubrics_metrics.description: What period have we now reached?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comprehension question assessing students' ability to identify the historical period covered in the preceding text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Question 2 (preceding CH. LI): Who were Governors at this time?
rubrics_metrics.description: Who were Governors at this time?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess recall of named state governors mentioned in the chapter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Question 3 (preceding CH. LI): What is said of Governor John Branch?
rubrics_metrics.description: What is said of Governor John Branch?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess understanding of the author's characterization of Governor John Branch.

rubrics_metrics.name: Question 4 (preceding CH. LI): What mention is made of the candidates for Governor?
rubrics_metrics.description: What mention is made of the candidates for Governor?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess recall and summarization of the gubernatorial candidates discussed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Question 5 (preceding CH. LI): What deaths of prominent men occurred about this period?
rubrics_metrics.description: What deaths of prominent men occurred about this period?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess ability to list notable deaths referenced and their significance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Question 6 (preceding CH. LI): What Governor was elected in 1844? How was he beloved in the State?
rubrics_metrics.description: What Governor was elected in 1844? How was he beloved in the State?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate knowledge of the 1844 gubernatorial election and the public perception of the victor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Question 7 (preceding CH. LI): What troubles arose in national matters on the election of James K. Polk?
rubrics_metrics.description: What troubles arose in national matters on the election of James K. Polk?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess comprehension of national events (e.g., Mexican War) tied to Polk's election.

rubrics_metrics.name: Question 8 (preceding CH. LI): What is said, of his visit to the University? Of what State was President Polk a native? How was his nomination announced?
rubrics_metrics.description: What is said, of his visit to the University? Of what State was President Polk a native? How was his nomination announced?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Checks multiple factual items about Polk: his university visit, birthplace, and the telegraphic announcement of his nomination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Question 9 (preceding CH. LI): Can you mention the North Carolina troops sent to Mexico, and their commanders?
rubrics_metrics.description: Can you mention the North Carolina troops sent to Mexico, and their commanders?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess recall of units and leaders from North Carolina involved in the Mexican War.

rubrics_metrics.name: Question 10 (preceding CH. LI): Tell something about Major Louis D. Wilson.
rubrics_metrics.description: Tell something about Major Louis D. Wilson.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess recall of biographical details and deeds of Major Louis D. Wilson as presented.

rubrics_metrics.name: Question 11 (preceding CH. LI): What valiant officer was with General Taylor at Buena Vista? Give an account of his timely aid to the American army.
rubrics_metrics.description: What valiant officer was with General Taylor at Buena Vista? Give an account of his timely aid to the American army.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate student's ability to recount the role of the named officer (e.g., Captain Braxton Bragg) and his actions at Buena Vista.

rubrics_metrics.name: Question 12 (preceding CH. LI): Describe the action.
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe the action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Open-ended prompt to summarize the battle/action described in the preceding narrative (Buena Vista).

rubrics_metrics.name: Question 13 (preceding CH. LI): What other officers are spoken of?
rubrics_metrics.description: What other officers are spoken of?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess recall of additional officers mentioned in the account.

rubrics_metrics.name: Question 1 (CH. LI): What is this lesson about? What is said of the period now reached?
rubrics_metrics.description: What is this lesson about? What is said of the period now reached?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Checks overall comprehension of Chapter LI's theme and its temporal framing (mid-1840s and social changes).

rubrics_metrics.name: Question 2 (CH. LI): How was North Carolina feeling the general impulse of improvement?
rubrics_metrics.description: How was North Carolina feeling the general impulse of improvement?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess understanding of North Carolina's response to mid-19th-century reform and improvement movements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Question 3 (CH. LI): In what condition were the railroads?
rubrics_metrics.description: In what condition were the railroads?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate recall of descriptions of the state's railroad infrastructure and its decay.

rubrics_metrics.name: Question 4 (CH. LI): How far west were the railroads reaching? Which of the roads was obtaining most travel?
rubrics_metrics.description: How far west were the railroads reaching? Which of the roads was obtaining most travel?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess knowledge of geographic extent of rail lines and which routes were most used (e.g., Wilmington Road).

rubrics_metrics.name: Question 5 (CH. LI): What important railway is now mentioned? What was to be its extent?
rubrics_metrics.description: What important railway is now mentioned? What was to be its extent?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Checks recall of the proposed North Carolina Railroad (Charlotte–Goldsboro) and its planned length (240 miles).

rubrics_metrics.name: Question 6 (CH. LI): Can you describe the passage of the 'Railroad Bill' through the Legislature?
rubrics_metrics.description: Can you describe the passage of the 'Railroad Bill' through the Legislature?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assesses ability to recount legislative debate, tie vote in Senate, and Calvin Graves' casting vote.

rubrics_metrics.name: Question 7 (CH. LI): What charitable institutions were provided for at this session? Through whose instrumentality was the appropriation made for the Insane Asylum?
rubrics_metrics.description: What charitable institutions were provided for at this session? Through whose instrumentality was the appropriation made for the Insane Asylum?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate recall of institutions (deaf/dumb/blind school, insane asylum) and Dorothea Dix's role.

rubrics_metrics.name: Question 8 (CH. LI): What devotion did Miss Dix give to this subject? What had been the disposition of the insane before this?
rubrics_metrics.description: What devotion did Miss Dix give to this subject? What had been the disposition of the insane before this?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess understanding of Dorothea Dix's advocacy and prior treatment of the mentally ill (jails, chains).

rubrics_metrics.name: Question 9 (CH. LI): What is said of these internal improvements?
rubrics_metrics.description: What is said of these internal improvements?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess synthesis of how railroads and institutions reflect civilization and humanity in the State.

rubrics_metrics.name: Question 10 (CH. LI): What other important law was enacted at this session? Can you tell something of the rights of married women previous to this time?
rubrics_metrics.description: What other important law was enacted at this session? Can you tell something of the rights of married women previous to this time?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Checks recall of married women's protection statute and prior husband-rights over wife's property and person.

rubrics_metrics.name: Question 11 (CH. LI): What were the provisions of the new law?
rubrics_metrics.description: What were the provisions of the new law?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess knowledge of specific legal protections introduced (wife's consent for sale of land, privy examination, abolition of corporal chastisement).

rubrics_metrics.name: Question 12 (CH. LI): What was indicated by these acts of the State?
rubrics_metrics.description: What was indicated by these acts of the State?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate student's interpretation of the broader social/political meaning of the legislative reforms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Question 13 (CH. LI): What reflections are made upon this era?
rubrics_metrics.description: What reflections are made upon this era?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Open question to summarize the author's reflective commentary on reform momentum and humanity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Question 1 (CH. LII): What educational institutions are mentioned?
rubrics_metrics.description: What educational institutions are mentioned?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess recall of named seminaries, colleges, and the University (e.g., Salem, Raleigh, Greensboro, Murfreesboro, Edgeworth Seminary, Wake Forest, Davidson, Trinity/Normal School).

rubrics_metrics.name: Question 2 (CH. LII): Who was Governor in 1818? What two men were distinguished in the United States Senate?
rubrics_metrics.description: Who was Governor in 1818? What two men were distinguished in the United States Senate?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Checks naming of governors and senators referenced (contextual dating may require review of prior chapter).

rubrics_metrics.name: Question 3 (CH. LII): Who were the representative men in the House?
rubrics_metrics.description: Who were the representative men in the House?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess recall of House members highlighted (e.g., James I. McKay, Kenneth Rayner, Thomas L. Clingman).

rubrics_metrics.name: Question 4 (CH. LII): Who succeeded Governor Graham in 1849? What proposition was agitating the people?
rubrics_metrics.description: Who succeeded Governor Graham in 1849? What proposition was agitating the people?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate understanding of Governor succession (Charles Manly then David S. Reid) and the suffrage/freehold qualification debate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Question 5 (CH. LII): Who succeeded James K. Polk as President of the United States? What is said of President Polk?
rubrics_metrics.description: Who succeeded James K. Polk as President of the United States? What is said of President Polk?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Checks knowledge that Gen. Taylor succeeded Polk and asks for author's characterization of Polk.

rubrics_metrics.name: Question 6 (CH. LII): What events were occurring in the West?
rubrics_metrics.description: What events were occurring in the West?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess recall of California gold discovery, statehood application, and implications for slavery question.

rubrics_metrics.name: Question 7 (CH. LII): What spectre of the past reappears? Relate circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.description: What spectre of the past reappears? Relate circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate student's ability to identify the return of slavery controversy after western expansion and related tensions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Question 8 (CH. LII): In what condition was the question now seen?
rubrics_metrics.description: In what condition was the question now seen?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess comprehension of how the slavery question was reframed by political events and compromises.

rubrics_metrics.name: Question 9 (CH. LII): What is said of the 'Wilmot Proviso' and 'Fugitive Slave Law'?
rubrics_metrics.description: What is said of the 'Wilmot Proviso' and 'Fugitive Slave Law'?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Checks understanding of these measures and their political reception in North and South.

rubrics_metrics.name: Question 10 (CH. LII): What was the 'Fugitive Slave Law'? How did the North legislate against this law of Congress?
rubrics_metrics.description: What was the'Fugitive Slave Law'? How did the North legislate against this law of Congress?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess knowledge of the law's provisions requiring return of escapees and Northern personal liberty laws enacted in response.

rubrics_metrics.name: Question 11 (CH. LII): How was the South affected by these troubles?
rubrics_metrics.description: How was the South affected by these troubles?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate ability to explain Southern reactions—exasperation, disheartenment, and questioning the Union's future.

rubrics_metrics.name: Question 1 (CH. LIII): Of what does this chapter treat ? How was the election of President, Pierce considered ?
rubrics_metrics.description: Of what does this chapter treat ? How was the election of President, Pierce considered ?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess comprehension of Chapter LIII's scope and contemporary Southern reaction to Pierce's election.

rubrics_metrics.name: Question 2 (CH. LIII): What is said of internal improvements?
rubrics_metrics.description: What is said of internal improvements?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate recall of developments such as railways, asylums, schools, and economic investment in industry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Question 3 (CH. LIII): What educational progress was being made?
rubrics_metrics.description: What educational progress was being made?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Checks knowledge of the Superintendent of Common Schools office, Calvin H. Wiley, Normal School powers, and Trinity College.

rubrics_metrics.name: Question 4 (CH. LIII): How was the value of lands increasing?
rubrics_metrics.description: How was the value of lands increasing?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess understanding of the economic effects of restored/new rail lines and improved agricultural practices (guano, compost).

rubrics_metrics.name: Question 5 (CH. LIII): What is said of the Presidential campaign of 1852?
rubrics_metrics.description: What is said of the Presidential campaign of 1852?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate recall of the fact that both vice-presidential candidates were North Carolina-born and educated at Chapel Hill.

rubrics_metrics.name: Question 6 (CH. LIII): In what condition were religious matters?
rubrics_metrics.description: In what condition were religious matters?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess understanding of church engagement in education and missionary activity, and denominational strains over slavery.

rubrics_metrics.name: Question 8 (CH. LIII): How was the question of slavery affecting some of the religious denominations?
rubrics_metrics.description: How was the question of slavery affecting some of the religious denominations?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Checks comprehension of divisions among Baptists and Methodists due to slavery controversies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Question 7 (CH. LIII): What new party was organized in Massachusetts? What was the main policy of the 'Know-Nothings'?
rubrics_metrics.description: What new party was organized in Massachusetts? What was the main policy of the 'Know-Nothings'?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess knowledge of the Know-Nothing/American Party and its nativist, anti-Catholic, anti-immigrant stances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Question 8 (CH. LIII): What is said of this new party?
rubrics_metrics.description: What is said of this new party?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate student's ability to summarize the author's critique of the Know-Nothings and their short-lived, pernicious effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Question 9 (CH. LIII): What party next originated?
rubrics_metrics.description: What party next originated?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Checks recall that the Republican Party arose in reaction to Kansas-Nebraska controversies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Question 10 (CH. LIII): How was the South affected by 'Squatter Sovereignty'?
rubrics_metrics.description: How was the South affected by 'Squatter Sovereignty'?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess understanding of how popular sovereignty threatened Southern settlers' security and led to conflict (e.g., Bleeding Kansas).

rubrics_metrics.name: Question 11 (CH. LIII): What fatal accident befell Dr. Elisha Mitchell in 1857?
rubrics_metrics.description: What fatal accident befell Dr. Elisha Mitchell in 1857?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Checks recall of Mitchell's death on Black Mountain and ensuing commemoration (Mitchell's Peak).

rubrics_metrics.name: Question 12 (CH. LIII): What changes in the government of the State are now mentioned?
rubrics_metrics.description: What changes in the government of the State are now mentioned?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess recall of political shifts and officeholders (e.g., Democratic gains, governors elected, senatorial changes).

rubrics_metrics.name: Question 1 (CH. LIV): How was the Presidential contest of 1860 viewed?
rubrics_metrics.description: How was the Presidential contest of 1860 viewed?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess comprehension of the 1860 election as a crisis signaling a supreme national crisis over slavery and constitutional authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Question 2 (CH. LIV): What was the issue? Who were the candidates; and what were their platforms?
rubrics_metrics.description: What was the issue? Who were the candidates; and what were their platforms?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate student's ability to name candidates (Lincoln, Douglas, Breckinridge, Bell) and summarize their positions on slavery/territories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Question 3 (CH. LIV): What was the real issue between the Democrats and Republicans? What views were held by each party?
rubrics_metrics.description: What was the real issue between the Democrats and Republicans? What views were held by each party?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Checks understanding of constitutional supremacy vs. higher unwritten law, and parties' stances regarding slavery and legal order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Question 4 (CH. LIV): To whom were most of the Southern people giving support? How did they view the probable election of Mr. Lincoln?
rubrics_metrics.description: To whom were most of the Southern people giving support? How did they view the probable election of Mr. Lincoln?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess recall that many Southerners supported Breckinridge/Lane and feared Lincoln's election as a precursor to Northern disregard for Southern rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Question 5 (CH. LIV): Who were elected? What did some of the Southern States intend to do?
rubrics_metrics.description: Who were elected? What did some of the Southern States intend to do?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate knowledge of Lincoln's election and early secessionist intentions among Southern states.

rubrics_metrics.name: Question 6 (CH. LIV): What occurred before the inauguration of Mr. Lincoln?
rubrics_metrics.description: What occurred before the inauguration of Mr. Lincoln?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess recall that seven states held conventions and declared ties to the Union dissolved prior to March 4, 1861.

rubrics_metrics.name: Question 7 (CH. LIV): What act was passed by the North Carolina Legislature?
rubrics_metrics.description: What act was passed by the North Carolina Legislature?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Checks recall of the 1 January 1861 act calling for a popular sense on holding a convention to consider the state's relations to the Union.

rubrics_metrics.name: Question 8 (CH. LIV): Can you tell the result of the vote upon this question?
rubrics_metrics.description: Can you tell the result of the vote upon this question?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess ability to report the close popular vote against holding a convention (majority of 194 against convention as officially counted).

rubrics_metrics.name: Question 9 (CH. LIV): What was the South beginning to realize?
rubrics_metrics.description: What was the South beginning to realize?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate understanding of shifting public sentiment toward unified Southern action and the imminence of secession.

rubrics_metrics.name: Question 10 (CH. LIV): What call was made upon North Carolina by Mr. Lincoln? With what result?
rubrics_metrics.description: What call was made upon North Carolina by Mr. Lincoln? With what result?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Checks recall that Lincoln requested troops to coerce seceded states and Governor Ellis refused the call, prompting mobilization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Question 11 (CH. LIV): When did North Carolina leave the Union?
rubrics_metrics.description: When did North Carolina leave the Union?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess recall that North Carolina's Ordinance of Secession was passed by the State Convention on May 20, 1861.

rubrics_metrics.name: Question 12 (CH. LIV): Can you repeat the Ordinance of Secession?
rubrics_metrics.description: Can you repeat the Ordinance of Secession?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tests knowledge of the ordinance's declarative language dissolving the Union and rescinding ratification of the U.S. Constitution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Question 13 (CH. LIV): Mention the political opinions to be found in the State upon these questions?
rubrics_metrics.description: Mention the political opinions to be found in the State upon these questions?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess student's ability to enumerate varied opinions (submissionists, separate-state action, concerted action, timing considerations).

rubrics_metrics.name: Question 14 (CH. LIV): What had been the hope of many of our people? How was the news of secession received?
rubrics_metrics.description: What had been the hope of many of our people? How was the news of secession received?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate comprehension of prior hopes for peaceful settlement and the popular reaction to secession (preparation for war).

rubrics_metrics.name: Question 15 (CH. LIV): What occurred on June 9th? Who succeeded Governor Ellis?
rubrics_metrics.description: What occurred on June 9th? Who succeeded Governor Ellis?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Checks recall of Governor Ellis's death on June 9, 1861 and succession by Henry Toole Clark (Speaker of the Senate).

rubrics_metrics.name: Question 16 (CH. LIV): What seizures were made by North Carolina authorities?
rubrics_metrics.description: What seizures were made by North Carolina authorities?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assesses knowledge of forts and federal arsenal seized (Forts Johnston, Macon, Caswell; Fayetteville arsenal) and arms captured.

rubrics_metrics.name: Question 17 (CH. LIV): What are the thoughts upon this period?
rubrics_metrics.description: What are the thoughts upon this period?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Open-ended synthesis question inviting reflection on North Carolina's patriotism and mobilization at the war's outbreak.

rubrics_metrics.name: Question 1 (CH. LV): How was the Presidential contest of 1860 viewed?
rubrics_metrics.description: How was the Presidential contest of 1860 viewed?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess comprehension of the 1860 election as indicating a supreme national crisis and the centrality of the slavery-in-territories issue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Question 2 (CH. LV): What was the issue? Who were the candidates; and what were their platforms?
rubrics_metrics.description: What was the issue? Who were the candidates; and what were their platforms?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Checks understanding of candidates (Lincoln, Douglas, Breckinridge, Bell), their stances on slavery, and the territorial question.

rubrics_metrics.name: Question 3 (CH. LV): What was the real issue between the Democrats and Republicans? What views were held by each party?
rubrics_metrics.description: What was the real issue between the Democrats and Republicans? What views were held by each party?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate comprehension of constitutional supremacy versus an asserted higher unwritten law and perceived threats to Southern rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Question 4 (CH. LV): To whom were most of the Southern people giving support? How did they view the probable election of Mr. Lincoln?
rubrics_metrics.description: To whom were most of the Southern people giving support? How did they view the probable election of Mr. Lincoln?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess recall that the South largely supported Breckinridge/Lane and feared that Lincoln's election would justify secession.

rubrics_metrics.name: Question 5 (CH. LV): Who were elected? What did some of the Southern States intend to do?
rubrics_metrics.description: Who were elected? What did some of the Southern States intend to do?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Checks knowledge that Lincoln won and that several Southern states planned/seized on secession.

rubrics_metrics.name: Question 6 (CH. LV): What occurred before the inauguration of Mr. Lincoln?
rubrics_metrics.description: What occurred before the inauguration of Mr. Lincoln?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess recall of secession ordinances and conventions held by Southern states prior to March 4, 1861.

rubrics_metrics.name: Question 7 (CH. LV): What act was passed by the North Carolina Legislature?
rubrics_metrics.description: What act was passed by the North Carolina Legislature?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Checks recall of the January 1, 1861 act authorizing a vote on whether the people should hold a convention regarding the Federal Union.

rubrics_metrics.name: Question 8 (CH. LV): Can you tell the result of the vote upon this question?
rubrics_metrics.description: Can you tell the result of the vote upon this question?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess ability to state the close official vote against holding the convention (45,509 for; 45,603 against; majority of 194 against).

rubrics_metrics.name: Question 9 (CH. LV): What was the South beginning to realize?
rubrics_metrics.description: What was the South beginning to realize?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate understanding of growing consensus for united Southern action as the only hope for future protection of rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Question 10 (CH. LV): What call was made upon North Carolina by Mr. Lincoln? With what result?
rubrics_metrics.description: What call was made upon North Carolina by Mr. Lincoln? With what result?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Checks recall that Lincoln's call for troops to coerce seceded states was refused by Governor Ellis, leading to mobilization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Question 11 (CH. LV): When did North Carolina leave the Union?
rubrics_metrics.description: When did North Carolina leave the Union?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess recall that the Ordinance of Secession was passed May 20, 1861.

rubrics_metrics.name: Question 12 (CH. LV): Can you repeat the Ordinance of Secession?
rubrics_metrics.description: Can you repeat the Ordinance of Secession?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tests reproduction/understanding of the ordinance's language dissolving the Union and rescinding prior ratification acts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Question 13 (CH. LV): Mention the political opinions to be found in the State upon these questions?
rubrics_metrics.description: Mention the political opinions to be found in the State upon these questions?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess ability to list and characterize the range of opinion in North Carolina regarding secession and timing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Question 14 (CH. LV): What had been the hope of many of our people? How was the news of secession received?
rubrics_metrics.description: What had been the hope of many of our people? How was the news of secession received?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate comprehension of initial hopes for peaceful adjustment and the widespread mobilization following secession.

rubrics_metrics.name: Question 15 (CH. LV): What occurred on June 9th? Who succeeded Governor Ellis?
rubrics_metrics.description: What occurred on June 9th? Who succeeded Governor Ellis?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Checks recall of Governor Ellis's death and succession by Henry Toole Clark.

rubrics_metrics.name: Question 16 (CH. LV): What seizures were made by North Carolina authorities?
rubrics_metrics.description: What seizures were made by North Carolina authorities?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess recall of captured forts and the Fayetteville arsenal, and the acquisition of arms and ammunition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Question 17 (CH. LV): What are the thoughts upon this period?
rubrics_metrics.description: What are the thoughts upon this period?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Open-ended prompt to reflect on North Carolina's patriotism, the scale of enlistment, and the state's role in the conflict's early phase.
